strategies.name: Sequential All-Reduce with Interleaved Scaling
strategies.desc: Performs 8 sequential all-reduce calls with element-wise scale/unscale operations between each. Each all-reduce operates on the full (W*S) vector. Results in 8 all-reduce dispatches plus 14 local elementwise kernels (7 scale + 7 unscale operations). Minimizes algorithmic complexity but maximizes dispatch count; represents the baseline reference pattern.

strategies.name: Fused Scale-AllReduce with Precomputed Buffers
strategies.desc: Pre-allocate and pre-fill scaling coefficient tensors, then fuse the scale-into-buffer operation with the all-reduce by issuing all 8 all-reduces back-to-back after preparing their input buffers in a single fused kernel. Results in 8 all-reduce dispatches plus 2 large fused local kernels (one for all scale operations, one for all unscale operations). Trades memory for reduced kernel launch overhead.

strategies.name: Reduce-Scatter + All-Gather Pipeline
strategies.desc: Replace each full-vector all-reduce with a reduce-scatter (producing local shard) followed by all-gather (broadcasting result). Apply per-shard scaling only on local S-sized chunks between stages. Results in 16 collective dispatches (8 RS + 8 AG) but each operates on smaller payloads; scales/unscales work on S-sized vectors. Better bandwidth utilization when network has high latency-to-bandwidth ratio.

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Level Reduction with Scale Factorization
strategies.desc: Exploit the fact that only 4 distinct scale values exist (a[r%4]). Group ranks by (r%4), perform 4-way intra-group all-reduce, apply group-specific scales, then perform cross-group reduction. Repeat for 8 stages using hierarchical topology. Reduces effective world size per collective from 224 to ~56, lowering per-all-reduce cost but requiring careful rank-group orchestration.

strategies.name: Batched All-Reduce with Concatenated Stage Vectors
strategies.desc:
Treat the 8 stages as a batch dimension: create an 8×(W*S) tensor where row i represents stage i's intermediate state. Issue a single large all-reduce on the entire concatenated payload, then separate and post-process. Results in 1 collective dispatch on 8× payload size plus complex local pre/post processing. Minimizes dispatch overhead at cost of 8× memory and potential network congestion.
